Definition: from G1223 and G2967; to hinder altogether, i.e. utterly prohibit:--forbid.
BiblicalUsage: To forbid altogether is to hinder completely, and John the Baptist does it once, when Jesus comes to be baptized. John forbids Him, saying he needs to be baptized by Jesus instead, and Jesus answers that it must be so to fulfil all righteousness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe John's forbidding shows how strange the gospel looks to a faithful man; the greater comes to the lesser to be baptized, and righteousness turns out to mean Jesus stepping into our place, not the other way around.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
